general_information.Description: This course will introduce the student to the essential aspects of information security and network forensics. The student will be provided with the tools, techniques and industry accepted methodologies so that upon completion of the course the student will be able to describe key concepts of network security and forensics and how those concepts apply to themselves and their organization. Assessment scheme: a) Ongoing assessment: 01 Midterm Test : 20%, Participation in discussions: 10%, 14 Labs: 40% b) Final examination (FE): 30% c) Completion criteria: Every on-going assessment component >0; Average Lab Score >= 4; Final Exam Score >=4 & Final Result >=5
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit in time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FPTU cms at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: Internet, WinPCap, Tcpdump, Wireshark, Tshark, dumpcap, TCPFlow, libpcap, NetworkMiner, Snort, Splunk, Yara, OpenID, SAML, LAMP

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: LO1: Provide an overview of current systems and infrastructures; describe key principles, such as defense in depth and demilitarized zones (DMZ)
LO2: Provide an overview of the requirement for intrusion detection systems (IDS) and their practical implementation; describe the principles regarding intrusion detection procedures.
LO3: Describe practical methods used in encryption, decryption, and authentication, including digital certificates and biometrics
LO4: Describe key concepts of secure code infrastructure
LO5: Provide an overview of network security devices and infrastructures, including proxy ,servers and firewalls
LO6: Describe network security risk and the range of threats

LO7: Describe the basic steps that an intruder might undertake in an intrusion; and provide a background and practical skills in the usage of vulnerability scanning and analysis. LO8: Describe the key network protocols, such as IP, TCP, ARP, ICMP, DNS, and the
LO8: Describe the key network protocols, such as IP, TCP, ARP, ICMP, DNS, and the methodologies used in network forensics
LO9: Describe data hiding and obfuscation and outline obfuscation methods
LO10: Provide an overview of web based architectures and define key protocols
LO11: Provide and introduction to cluster, grid and cloud infrastructures

assessments.Grading Guide: - Guided by instructor - 14 Lab-Projects are arranged relevant to the chapter theory - Student must finish labs and submit the results to the lecturer in class. - An average point of all labs could be evaluated and published to students at the end of the semester

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choices Marked by Computer or a suitable format
assessments.Note: Instruction and schedules for Progress Tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by director of the campus. The test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has responsibility to review the test for students after graded.

schedule.Topic: Lecture 1. Introduction to Security 1.1 Overview of Key Terms (C-I-A, AAA, ...) 1.2 Overview of Current Systems and Infrastructures (with cloud computing, ...) 1.3 Information Security and Forensic Computing 1.4 Defining Key Principles (Defense-in-Depth, DMZ, ...) 1.5 Python Coding for Network Packet Capture
Lab 1: Data Packet Capture (Network Interface, Filtering, IDS, ARP, ...)

Lecture 2. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) 2.1 Overview of the Requirement for IDS and Their Use 2.2 Practical Implementation of IDS Using Snort 2.3 Typical Detection Procedures (for ping sweeps, ...).
Lab 2: Using Snort to Detect Attacks

Lecture 3. Encryption, Authentication, Hashing, and Digital Certificates 3.1 Overview of the Methods Used in Symmetric and Asymmetric Encryption 3.2 How to Crack Encrypted Content 3.3 Range of Standard Encryption Methods 3.4 Overview of Authentication Methods, Including the Usage of Biometrics 3.5 Usage of Digital Certificates in Private Key Signing 3.6 Integrating Hash Methods and Their Applications
Lab-Project 3: Encryption, Hashing Cracking, PGP, Cracking Digital Certificates and File Types

Lecture 4. Enhanced Software Security 4.1 Best Practice of Software Security and the Future 4.2 Overview of a Secure Code Infrastructure Focusing on Microsoft .NET 4.3 Key Concepts of Security within the Microsoft .NET Infrastructure
Lab 4: Role-Based Security

Lecture 5. Network Security Elements 5.1 Overview of Security Devices and Infrastructures 5.2 Router (Packet Filtering) Firewalls 5.3 Network Address Translation (NAT) 5.4 PIX/ASA Firewall 5.5 Proxy Servers
Lab-Project 5: Creating Secure Architectures
Lecture 6. Introduction to Risk 6.1 Security Taxonomy 6.2 Threats 6.3 Service-Oriented Infrastructures 6.4 Practical Background in Windows and Linux for Services, Logging, and Auditing
Lab 6: Log, Process, Hashing

Lecture 7. Threat Analysis 7.1 Intruder Detection 7.2 Vulnerably Analysis 7.3 Hping, Botnets, Pbisbing 7.4 Buffer Overflows and Cross-Scripting (XSS) 7.5 Inference and Affiliate Scams 7.6 Password Cracking Programs
Lab-Project 7: Advanced Network Attack Analysis
Lectures 8. Network Forensics 1 8.1 The Key Protocols 8.2 Ethernet, IP, and TCP Headers 8.3 TCP Connection 8.4 ARP and SYN
Lab 8: Network Packet Inspection
Lectures 9. Network Forensics 2 9.1 Application Layer Analysis-FTP 8.2 ICMP and DNS LO8 8.3 Port Scan and SYN Flood 8.4 Spoofed Addresses
Lab 9: Network Packet Analysis
Lectures 10. Network Forensics 3 10.1 Application Layer Analysis-HTTP 10.2 Network Logs on Hosts 10.3 Tripwire
Lab 10: Tripwire, Log and Packet Analysis
